column4: Hell is both a bed beneath and غَوَاشٍ above its people, an exact root-family image of punitive coverings enclosing them.
A kindled fire lights everything around the hypocrites, then God removes their light and leaves them in darkness unable to see; disclosure is deliberately reversed into covering.
Lightning almost takes their sight: they walk whenever it illuminates them and stop when darkness covers them, making action depend moment by moment on disclosure.
Night cannot outstrip day, and all the heavenly bodies move in ordered courses; this completes the skin-peeling transition of 36:37 with its measured boundary.
God makes night and day successors to one another for whoever will remember or give thanks, presenting each as the other's recurring replacement.
Moses sees a fire and expects either news or a burning brand, another scene in which distant fire promises perception, direction, and aid.
Moses perceives fire from the side of the mountain and seeks news or a brand from it, repeating the meeting of sight, fire, and guidance.
The storm parable surrounds people with darkness, thunder, and lightning; it supplies the enveloping scene in which the intermittent visibility of 2:20 operates.
God gathers and layers clouds, sends hail, and the flash of their lightning nearly takes sight; clouded heaven produces a blinding brilliance opposite the dictionary's clear sky.
Some faces on that Day are bright, supplying the positive face-scene opposite the dust-covered faces of 80:40.
Those bright faces laugh and rejoice, completing their visible state before 80:40-41 turns to the darkened faces.
Under the غاشية, humbled faces are عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ, laboring and exhausted; the overwhelming event exposes one outcome of human striving.
The joyful faces are satisfied with their striving, لِّسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ, directly revealing the contrary outcome of the سعي named in 92:4.
Every messenger speaks his people's language so he can make the message clear, after which God misguides or guides; clarification and guidance are explicitly sequenced.
God sends clarifying signs and guides whom He wills to a straight path, another direct pairing of disclosure and huda.
The Quran is sent as clear signs, followed by the statement that God guides whom He wills, matching the section's bayan sense of huda.
The Prophet cannot guide whom he loves; God alone guides whom He wills and knows the guided, delimiting the divine claim that guidance belongs to Him.
God guides the human being to the two elevated ways, giving the disclosed path the two-way moral divergence announced after 92's opening oaths.
Moses identifies the Lord as the One who gives every created thing its form and then guides it, joining creation directly to guidance.
God creates and proportions; 87:3 continues this ordered making with measuring and guidance, paralleling the movement from 92:3 to 92:12.
God measures and then guides, وَٱلَّذِى قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ, presenting huda as part of making creation fit and ordered.
When Israel demands to see God openly, the thunderbolt seizes them, a human counterpart to the mountain's inability to bear divine disclosure in 7:143.
God rolls up heaven like a written scroll and recreates it, turning the world's upper covering into a layer visibly folded away.
The challengers demand that a spring gush from the earth; 17:91 expands that breach into rivers running through gardens.
Moses strikes the stone and twelve springs burst from it, a precise water-cleaving-solid-matter scene related to the river that cuts earth.
The repeated Moses scene has the struck rock send forth twelve springs, preserving the image of water opening a hard surface.
Those reminded of God's signs turn away while coverings remain over their hearts and heaviness in their ears, explicitly joining warning to sealed perception.
For those enclosed and covered in 36:9, warning and silence are equal; this ayah states the practical effect of their inability to see.
Warning benefits the one who follows the reminder and fears the Merciful unseen, the receptive counterpart to the covered people of 36:9-10.
God brings out what is hidden in the heavens and earth and knows what people conceal and disclose, directly casting guidance as emergence from concealment.
At judgment there appears to evildoers from God what they had never reckoned with, a disclosure of reality previously hidden from their expectations.
The evils they earned become manifest and the mocked punishment encloses them, combining disclosure of deeds with an engulfing consequence.
The human being labors toward the Lord and will meet Him, another concise statement of striving moving toward eventual disclosure and encounter.
God distinguishes the corrupt from the good and gathers each kind, making previously intermixed human courses visibly separate.
When the Hour rises, people split apart, another direct eschatological disclosure of the divergence modeled by opening daylight.
Whichever way people turn, there is the Face of God, broadening the sought divine Face beyond one physical direction.
The warning fire is لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ, scorching or blackening skin, a concrete Quranic counterpart to the section's wick-soot used as a bodily mark.
A condemned person can only shield the face from the punishment, reversing the ordinary relation by making the face itself the last covering before fire.
Hypocrites ask believers to wait so they can borrow light, but a wall with mercy inside and punishment outside divides them; illumination reveals the final boundary.
The Fire sees its people from a distant place before they reach it, reversing the Moses scenes in which a person sees distant fire and approaches it for guidance.
The alternation of night and day and all God created are signs for the mindful, placing the pair within the same created order as 92:3.
Creation of heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day are signs, another explicit conjunction of creation with the opening pair.
The alternation of night and day appears among created signs for people who reason, locating the visual cycle within a field of divine evidence.
The alternation of night and day is joined to provision that revives dead earth, so cosmic disclosure is paired with emergence from lifeless ground.
God gives life and death and controls the alternation of night and day, connecting the daily change to the larger passage between hiddenness and emergence.
God creates night and day, sun and moon, each moving in an orbit; this supplies the ordered created motion behind their repeated covering and opening.
Night, day, sun, moon, and stars are subjected by God's command, reinforcing that the two operations belong to the created order He governs.
Night and day are named as divine signs alongside sun and moon, and worship is directed to their Creator rather than the visible signs.
The Quran is sent down in a blessed night, a specific counterexample to treating night-cover as intrinsically adverse.
On Resurrection Day the faces of those who lied about God are blackened, another visible facial outcome disclosed at judgment.
Believing men and women have light running before them and on their right on the Day of judgment, the illumination withheld from hypocrites in 57:13.
A manifest proof and clear light come from the Lord, bringing the section's opposed families of hiddenness and illumination into revelation language.
God promises believers a light by which they may walk, joining divine mercy, movement, and opened sight.
Believers' light runs before them on the Day they ask God to perfect it, presenting final safety as completed illumination.
The Prophet is sent as a luminous lamp, making warning and invitation themselves a source of light.
On reaching the fire Moses is called and the fire's surroundings are blessed, completing the revelatory outcome of the distant sight in 27:7.
At the fire Moses is called from a tree in the blessed valley, completing the movement from visible fire in 28:29 to divine address.
The sky splits and becomes frail on the Last Day, another concrete breach of the upper covering.
The sky splits and becomes rose-red like oil, giving the opening of heaven a vivid transformed surface.
The struck sea splits and each part rises like a mountain, extending the section's cleaving action from earth and dawn to water.
Abundant water is poured before the earth is split in 80:26, identifying what enables the hidden growth to emerge through that breach.
Warning and not warning are equal for the rejecters; 2:7 then locates the obstruction in sealed faculties and the veil over their eyes.
Whoever is blind in this life remains blind and further astray in the next, linking present covered perception to its revealed consequence.
The servants of the Merciful do not respond to reminders by collapsing as though deaf and blind, a receptive reversal of willfully covered perception.
After graves and breasts are opened in 100:9-10, their Lord is fully aware of them that Day, completing the disclosure scene.
Criminals are commanded to separate themselves on that Day, making the divergence of human courses an explicit visible division.
God will not leave believers in their present mixed state until He distinguishes the corrupt from the good, another disclosure of difference beneath apparent sameness.
Branding the offender upon the snout may faintly echo the section's secondary soot-as-tattoo image, though this ayah does not state the branding medium.
